summary: Backend-only public API authorization regression executed twice: 13/18 passed each run, five deterministic failures. Core records verification/membership, scoped UTC consent, revocation, patient ownership and scheduled/completed relationship checks pass. Offset expiry and adjacent clinical-route authorization remain unsafe. No product code changed.

critical.issue: Consent with +10:00 expiry still authorizes chart after the actual expiry instant (200 instead of 403). Reproduced twice using a grant expiring in two seconds and waiting three seconds.

Unverified doctor with a scheduled appointment reads another patient's synthetic lab document (200 instead of 403). OCR authorization checks appointment relationship but not approval or active membership. Reproduced twice.

Approved doctor without active membership reads an appointment plus enriched patient data (200 instead of 403). Endpoint uses get_current_user without professional verification/membership enforcement. Reproduced twice.

Timezone-free ISO expiry produces HTTP 500 instead of validation 400/422. Backend logs confirm TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes at consents/router.py:18. Reproduced twice.

minor.issue: Valid consent expiring one hour in the future represented in -10:00 timezone is denied (403 instead of 200). Same string-comparison root cause as expired-consent bypass; reproduced twice.

action_items: Validate timezone-aware consent expiry; normalize expiry to UTC before storage and compare actual instants. Handle existing offset-formatted grants safely, without broad destructive migration.
Apply central professional approval/membership checks to OCR document reads/reviews/downloads and professional appointment/consultation/billing/task reads, not only require_role endpoints.
Use central scope-aware chart decisions consistently; retain scheduled/completed relationship semantics and patient self-access.
Rerun test_clinical_authorization.py after fixes; add direct review/download and consultation/task regression coverage.
critical_code_review_comments: access.py:26-27 compares expires_at strings against UTC ISO text; grant router stores original body.expires_at despite parsing it. ISO text with arbitrary offsets is not chronologically sortable.

ocr/router.py:54-60 duplicates chart authorization, omits require_verified_member and ignores scoped consent. Both document review and file download reuse this vulnerable helper; these two operations were reviewed but not executed.

appointments/mine uses get_current_user and enriches with complete user objects minus password_hash. consultations create/list/get/join, billing invoice reads and partner-task mine similarly lack central professional approval/membership gates (code-only beyond executed appointment test).
Consent grant/revoke does not write audit events, unlike record creation and professional verification. Clinical consent lifecycle should be auditable.

Existing test_partner_access.py assumes only patients may self-register and partner self-record reads return 200; those assertions are stale under the new pending-professional signup and chart safety policy. Do not interpret that old suite unchanged as this feature's acceptance test.
test_credentials: Read documented credentials and auth instructions first. Documented patient, doctor and admin logins succeeded; no existing account modified. Credentials are not reproduced in this report.
seed_data_creation: No seed/reset/migration. Each run created nine isolated TEST_ accounts using public signup, approved two through admin API, created one TEST_ organization and one active membership through public API, and created records/consents through public APIs. Synthetic appointment, inactive-membership and lab-document database fixtures enabled isolated authorization checks without external booking/OCR integrations. All test fixtures cleaned up only by captured IDs; user/identity, consent and record absence assertions passed. Normal audit events retained. No APIs MOCKED.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Source frontend/.env, then run pytest backend/tests/test_clinical_authorization.py -v --tb=short --junitxml=test_reports/pytest/clinical_authorization_retest.xml. Tests have 18 functions, module-isolated setup and finally cleanup; consent cases revoke their own grant. Public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL used for every HTTP call. Mongo config is read only from protected backend env for synthetic setup/cleanup. No UI or external OAuth/LLM/storage integrations exercised. Date calculations use runtime UTC (container date November 2026), not hardcoded dates. Available finish tool substitutes for unavailable test_finish; auth integration-playbook tool unavailable. Prior auth lockout/cookie issues were not rerun in this scoped authorization regression.
rca of the issue: Expiry bypass: grant +2 seconds converted to +10:00, wait 3 seconds, doctor GET records returns 200 because local timestamp string sorts after current UTC. False denial: future +1 hour grant converted to -10:00 sorts before UTC. Naive expiry: datetime.fromisoformat accepts no-offset text then comparison raises unhandled TypeError. OCR bypass: synthetic scheduled relationship and pending doctor token satisfy relationship-only helper. Appointment leak: approved nonmember token satisfies get_current_user and receives enriched clinical queue without a professional gate.
